old_values: IGF-1 LR3 is an 83-amino acid synthetic analog of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) with a modified N-terminus. The arginine-to-glutamate substitution at position 3 and 13-amino acid extension significantly reduces IGF binding protein affinity, resulting in enhanced and prolonged biological activity compared to native IGF-1.
description.new_value: IGF-1 LR3 (LR3-IGF-I) is an 83-amino-acid analogue of human insulin-like growth factor 1. Arginine replaces glutamate at position 3 (Glu3→Arg), and a 13-amino-acid N-terminal extension is added. In laboratory studies these changes lower binding to IGF-binding proteins. WADA prohibits IGF-1 analogues. Research use only.

old_values: IGF-1 LR3 (Long R3 Insulin-like Growth Factor-1) is an 83-amino acid synthetic analog of human IGF-1. It was developed by modifying the native IGF-1 sequence — substituting a glutamic acid for the arginine at position 3 and adding a 13-amino acid N-terminal extension peptide. These modifications dramatically reduce binding to IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), which normally sequester circulating IGF-1 and limit its bioavailability. As a result, IGF-1 LR3 maintains significantly higher biological potency and an extended half-life compared to native IGF-1. Originally developed as a research tool for studying IGF-1 signaling pathways, IGF-1 LR3 has become widely used in cell culture applications where it promotes cellular proliferation and inhibits apoptosis more effectively than standard IGF-1.
background.new_value: IGF-1 LR3 (Long R3 Insulin-like Growth Factor-1) is an 83-amino acid synthetic analog of human IGF-1. It was developed by modifying the native IGF-1 sequence — replacing the glutamic acid at position 3 with arginine (Glu3→Arg) and adding a 13-amino acid N-terminal extension peptide. These modifications dramatically reduce binding to IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), which normally sequester circulating IGF-1 and limit its bioavailability. As a result, IGF-1 LR3 maintains significantly higher biological potency and an extended half-life compared to native IGF-1. Originally developed as a research tool for studying IGF-1 signaling pathways, IGF-1 LR3 has become widely used in cell culture applications where it promotes cellular proliferation and inhibits apoptosis more effectively than standard IGF-1.

description.target: education_posts.description of the category-linked post; if that is NULL/empty after normalize, product_categories.description of the same category (the controller fallback). Never both.
old_values:
Retatrutide is a triple agonist targeting GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors simultaneously. Phase 2 data showed up to 24% weight reduction — the highest of any peptide compound studied.

As of early October 2026, retatrutide remains investigational: not FDA-approved and not commercially marketed by the sponsor. Lilly has stated a plan to submit a U.S. BLA in Q1 2027 while completing CMC (filing plan ≠ acceptance ≠ approval). A Seventh Circuit oral argument on biologic classification (Eli Lilly v. Kennedy, No. 26-1301, 24 Sep 2026) was held; no ruling was located as of early Oct 2026.
description.new_value:
Retatrutide is an investigational triple agonist targeting GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors. Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 and TRIUMPH-2 results were published on 29 Sep 2026 (NEJM; The Lancet). Weight-change figures on the encyclopedia page are labeled by trial and estimand and are not head-to-head comparisons with other compounds.

As of 22 October 2026, retatrutide remains investigational: not FDA-approved and not commercially marketed by the sponsor. Lilly has said it plans to file a U.S. application no later than Q1 2027 (filing plan ≠ acceptance ≠ approval). On 2 October 2026, on remand, FDA concluded that retatrutide is not a biological product and that an application would go under section 505 (the drug pathway). Lilly’s related Seventh Circuit appeal (Eli Lilly v. Kennedy, No. 26-1301; oral argument 24 Sep 2026) had no ruling as of 22 Oct 2026.

sources: Text identical to 2026_10_22_160000 target; sources in reta-s505-2026-10-22-CHANGES.md (TRIUMPH-1 NEJM 29 Sep 2026; TRIUMPH-2 Lancet; FDA remand decision 2 Oct 2026; 7th Cir. No. 26-1301)
